messages:
sam: Ok team — proposing a new traffic generator variant: 'qps-mosaic'. Goal: combine gradual ramps, interleaved short stochastic microbursts, and explicit KV-warmup windows so we can reproduce long-tail regressions reliably. Thoughts?
anya: nice. can it _force_ prefix KV hits before the ramp? that has bitten us in the past where warmup was implicit.
kevin: yes, we need an explicit KV-warmup phase + steady-state + randomized spikes. also add kernel-selection toggles in the harness so we can compare apples-to-apples (int8 vs fp16 vs fallback kernels).
maria: if we do that, include a mode that pins sequence length distribution (short/med/long) per phase so batching heuristics behave like real workloads. otherwise data skews the batching profiles.
sam: agreed. rough config sketch: ```yaml
phases:
  - name: kv_warmup
    duration_s: 60
    qps: 50
    seq_len_dist: low
    kv_prefix: true
  - name: ramp_up
    duration_s: 120
    start_qps: 50
    end_qps: 400
    pattern: sawtooth
  - name: steady_mosaic
    duration_s: 600
    base_qps: 200
    stochastic_spikes:
      rate_per_min: 6
      spike_qps: 1500
      spike_dur_s: 2-6
    seq_len_dist: mixed
  - name: cooldown
    duration_s: 60
    qps: 20
    kv_prefix: false
```
raj: perfbot: can we get a quick run with kernel toggles on the canary fleet? want to measure batching depth and KV hit ratios. perfbot: queued: run id 2026-03-qps-mosaic-01, kernels: [fast-gemm, fallback], log level: info.
perfbot: result (summary): run 2026-03-qps-mosaic-01 complete. p50=7.6ms, p95=44.2ms, p99=123.8ms. KV hit ratio: 0.72. avg batching depth: 6.1 tokens/batch.
kevin: interesting — p99 is high during microbursts. can we correlate with kernel selection logs? maybe we fell back to safe kernels under burst backpressure.
anya: attaching a snippet from the runtime profiler: ```text
[00:03:12] kernel_select: model=xl-8q, seq=128 -> selected=fast-gemm
[00:03:13] kernel_select: model=xl-8q, seq=128 -> fallback=slow-token
[00:03:13] batcher: queue_len=320, batch_size=1 -> flush_reason=latency_slo
[00:03:13] kv_cache: miss -> backend_fetch 14ms
```
maria: that flush_reason line is the smoking gun — batching depth collapsed during the spike because latency SLO forced flushes, causing many single-token batches which hit fallback kernels. We should experiment with softer latency slack to allow batching to build.
sam: proposal: add an 'elastic_latency_window' param to traffic generator so we can sweep tolerance (0..50ms) and measure batching depth vs p99. Also add 'kv-splay' which staggers KV prefetch to avoid thundering.
kevin: also include a 'kernel_hold' feature: if a fast kernel was used in the last N requests for a route, prefer it for M seconds unless error rate spikes. helps avoid oscillation in selection.
anya: for apples-to-apples comparisons, we must freeze everything but the kernel binary. same seed for random spikes, fixed warmup. log format: include seed, config checksum, and runtime kernel hashes.
raj: running a controlled sweep: seeds [42, 43, 44], elastic_latency_window [0,10,25,50], kernel_policy [hold_on, immediate]. expect 12 runs per canary.
perfbot: queued: sweep id qps-mosaic-sweep-311. estimated runtime 3h. will upload per-run artifacts to s3://redwood-perf/qps-mosaic/311/
sam: one more thought — add a 'tail-sculpt' option: after each spike, generate a decaying Poisson tail to mimic downstream queuing and KV backend jitter. that will surface real p99 tail behavior rather than just instant spikes.
maria: agreed. also capture GPU kernel durations at sub-ms resolution and correlate with batch sizes in the tracer. if we see stragglers in GPU op times, we might have a reproducible kernel regression.
kevin: if p99 regresses >10% on identical seeds and kernel hashes, mark as perf-regression and auto-open a jira with attached logs + minimal repro (single-run config).
anya: can we add a tiny UI preview in console to visualize the QPS mosaic before running? quick ascii: base ramp + random spike ticks + long-tail decay. makes it easier for PMs to describe tests.
sam: love that. next steps: I will PR the traffic generator changes (kv_warmup, elastic_latency_window, kernel_hold, tail_sculpt) and a canonical config for apples-to-apples runs. assigning reviewers @anya @kevin. :rocket:
anya: ack, i'll review tomorrow.
kevin: will add kernel hash capture and adjust tracer.
raj: will queue the sweep after PR is merged.
perfbot: note: include perf regression alert thresholds in metadata: p99_delta_pct=10, p95_delta_pct=15.
sam: thanks all — aim to validate on canary this week and narrow down the regression root cause if it reproduces.
